high.title: New SBV Circular Raises Short-Term Capital for Medium/Long-Term Lending Ratio Cap Back to 40%, Adjusts LDR Calculation — Multiple Bank Stocks to Benefit
high.summary:
The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has issued a new circular making two significant regulatory adjustments to the banking sector. First, the cap on the Short-term Funding for Long-term Lending ratio (SFL) has been **raised from 30% back to 40%** — a complete policy reversal from the progressive tightening cycle maintained since 2019, which had gradually reduced the ceiling from 40% down to 30% (effective October 2023). This signals a decisive pivot toward prioritizing credit growth support over structural liquidity prudence, reflecting the economy's need for longer-duration investment capital. Second, the new circular adjusts the Loan-to-Deposit Ratio (LDR) calculation methodology by continuing to exclude non-term State Treasury deposits from the denominator while **newly permitting exclusion of 80% of term State Treasury deposits**. This technical adjustment meaningfully benefits banks with large government budget deposit balances. For bond and equity investors, this easing cycle has direct implications: expanded medium/long-term lending capacity could support credit growth momentum, compress funding costs, and positively re-rate bank stocks. Watch for potential steepening of deposit rate competition and its secondary effect on VND liquidity conditions.

high.title: VNDirect Forecasts VN-Index Could Break 2,000 Points; Identifies Sectors "Still in Play" for H2 2026
high.summary:
VNDirect Securities has released an updated macro and market strategy report, projecting the VN-Index could breach the psychologically significant 2,000-point level in H2 2026. The brokerage argues that Vietnamese equities endured a challenging first half shaped by global macro headwinds, but underlying economic resilience remains intact. Key catalysts identified for the second half include: (1) **FTSE Russell's official market upgrade decision**, which is expected to unlock substantial passive and active foreign inflows into Vietnamese equities; (2) ongoing market infrastructure reforms improving settlement and custody frameworks; and (3) a stable macroeconomic backdrop supporting corporate earnings growth. VNDirect forecasts listed companies on HoSE could deliver **net profit growth of up to 21% in 2026**, with broad-based gains across multiple key sectors. For international fund managers, the FTSE upgrade catalyst is the most critical variable to monitor — confirmation would trigger meaningful capital flow reallocation into VN equities, with secondary positive effects on VND demand and local bond markets. Watch for FTSE Russell's formal announcement timeline and any SBV commentary on managing potential capital inflow pressures.

---

medium.title: H1 2026 Investment Channel Performance Review: Gold and Silver Underperform
medium.summary:
A mid-year performance review of major asset classes reveals a notable divergence in H1 2026. Brent crude led all assets with a +16.6% gain, while US equities also posted strong returns. In contrast, gold fell approximately 7% and silver declined 17.1% from their January historical peaks — the worst-performing assets surveyed. The primary drivers cited are a strengthening USD and persistently elevated US Treasury yields, as the Federal Reserve has not yet signaled a pivot toward monetary easing. For Vietnam specifically, the VN-Index returned only 4.2% over the first half, marginally outperforming 6-month bank deposit rates. The article implicitly highlights that Vietnamese retail investors rotating between savings deposits and equities face a low-return environment. The Fed's hawkish hold is a key macro variable to monitor, as it sustains USD strength, which historically pressures the VND and complicates SBV's FX management. Bond investors should note that a prolonged high-rate environment in the US limits Vietnam's room to cut domestic rates without exacerbating VND depreciation pressure.

medium.title: Good News for Bank and Finance Company Borrowers: SBV Circular 29/2026 Raises Small Loan Thresholds and Changes Overdue Debt Collection Order
medium.summary: The SBV has issued Circular 29/2026/TT-NHNN (signed by Deputy Governor Pham Thanh Ha on June 30, 2026), amending Circular 39/2016 governing lending activities by credit institutions. Key changes include: (1) **raising the "small-value loan" threshold** from unspecified prior levels to VND 200 million at People's Credit Funds and VND 400 million at other credit institutions — reducing administrative burden and potentially stimulating retail credit demand; and (2) **changing overdue debt repayment priority to principal-first, interest-second**, a consumer-friendly adjustment that lowers the effective interest burden for distressed borrowers. While primarily a consumer protection and credit access measure, this circular is relevant for banking sector analysts as it may modestly support loan growth at the retail and micro-lending segment, with positive read-through for consumer finance companies. Watch for potential impact on non-performing loan (NPL) recovery dynamics under the new repayment waterfall.

medium.title: Domestic Gold Prices Continue to Fall on July 1st Morning — Bar and Ring Gold Both Down
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices fell uniformly on the morning of July 1st, with major dealers SJC, PNJ, DOJI, and Bao Tin Manh Hai all reducing prices by VND 0.6 million/tael across both buy and sell sides. SJC gold bars were quoted at VND 143.4–146.4 million/tael (buy–sell), while ring gold similarly declined. The move tracked international spot gold, which fell 0.9% to USD 3,972/ounce during the Asian session. While a gold price article, the domestic gold-USD spread and gold market dynamics in Vietnam remain a secondary indicator of VND sentiment and local safe-haven demand — relevant context for FX traders monitoring capital flight proxies.

medium.title: Goods and Services Prices Skyrocket Following Fuel Prices; Fuel Prices Fall, But Sellers Stubbornly Hold Prices High
medium.summary:
This article highlights a classic asymmetric price-stickiness dynamic in Vietnam's consumer economy. When fuel prices surged due to Middle East conflict (approximately three months ago), food and service vendors in Ho Chi Minh City quickly passed costs through to consumers — raising prices on staple items such as pho (VND 45,000–60,000/bowl), rice dishes (VND 60,000–70,000), and transport fees. However, with fuel prices now falling sharply following the US-Iran ceasefire and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, vendors are refusing to reverse those price increases.

**Relevance to Fund Managers:** This price stickiness is a meaningful input for Vietnam's CPI trajectory. If service-sector prices remain elevated despite falling energy input costs, headline inflation may prove more persistent than the SBV's models anticipate. Sticky core inflation would complicate any potential monetary easing cycle and could delay rate cuts. Bond investors should monitor upcoming CPI prints closely — if inflation remains above target, the SBV will have limited room to cut policy rates, keeping the short end of the yield curve supported. FX implications are secondary but worth watching: persistent inflation differentials with the US could maintain VND depreciation pressure.

medium.title: Losing Sleep After Buying Gold at VND 190 Million/Tael — Three Hard-Won Lessons
medium.summary:
This personal finance piece describes an individual investor who purchased domestic gold (SJC) near the peak price of VND 190 million per tael, driven by FOMO rather than a structured investment plan. The author reflects on the emotional toll of price-watching and the absence of any exit strategy or liquidity planning.

**Relevance to Fund Managers:** While anecdotal, this article is a useful sentiment indicator for Vietnamese retail investor behavior. Domestic gold at VND 190 million/tael represents an extraordinary premium to international spot prices, reflecting capital flight dynamics, SBV supply constraints, and deep distrust of VND as a store of value. Widespread retail gold buying at peak prices — without clear strategy — suggests frothy sentiment in the gold market and potential for sharp corrections. For FX traders, sustained retail demand for gold in VND is a structural source of USD demand pressure (given gold import linkages), which the SBV must manage through intervention and supply quotas.

medium.title: Why You Shouldn't Only Deposit Money at the Bank with the Highest Interest Rate?
medium.summary: As of early July 2026, several Vietnamese banks continue to offer elevated deposit rates targeted at large depositors, providing a useful read on the current retail funding environment. PVcomBank leads the market with rates up to **10%/year** for 12–13 month tenors, though this applies exclusively to deposits of VND 2,000 billion or more — effectively institutional-only. MSB follows at **9%/year** for 12–13 month deposits (minimum VND 500 billion), while Nam A Bank offers **8.3%/year** for 24-month deposits above VND 500 billion. The persistence of high headline deposit rates at smaller and mid-tier banks signals continued competition for liquidity, which is relevant for monitoring funding costs across the sector. For bond investors, elevated deposit rates at the longer end (12–24 months) suggest the market is not yet pricing in near-term rate cuts, and may exert upward pressure on short-to-medium tenor government bond yields. The tiered and restrictive access conditions also suggest these are wholesale funding tools rather than broad monetary signals.

medium.title: VPBank Tops Private Banks in Forbes Global 2000 Rankings
medium.summary: VPBank (HoSE: VPB) has been ranked **#1,373 on the Forbes Global 2000** for 2026, climbing 257 places from its 2025 position of #1,630 and marking its third consecutive year on the list. Notably, VPBank now ranks as the **highest-placed Vietnamese private commercial bank** on the list, reflecting strong growth in scale, financial capacity, and operational efficiency. For equity investors tracking the Vietnamese banking sector, VPBank's rising global profile may enhance its attractiveness to foreign institutional investors, particularly in the context of the anticipated FTSE Russell upgrade which could drive incremental passive and active flows into large-cap Vietnamese bank stocks. This is a positive signal for VPB's stock and indirectly for broader banking sector sentiment on the VN-Index.

medium.title: Prime Minister Appoints New Director General of Vietnam Bank for Social Policies
medium.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Nguyen Van Thang signed Decision No. 1169/QĐ-TTg on June 29, appointing **Ms. Nguyen Thi Hang** as Director General and Board Member of the Vietnam Bank for Social Policies (VBSP), effective July 1, 2026. Ms. Hang (born 1978, Bac Ninh province) holds master's and bachelor's degrees in law, economics, and finance-banking, and previously served as Deputy Director General of VBSP and Director of its Ninh Binh branch. While VBSP is a policy bank focused on social lending rather than commercial operations, leadership transitions at state-directed financial institutions are worth monitoring for any shifts in directed credit policy or funding mandates that could affect overall banking sector liquidity conditions.

medium.title: Fuel Prices Uniformly Reduced from the Afternoon of July 2nd
medium.summary:
The Ministry of Industry and Trade together with the Ministry of Finance conducted a periodic fuel price adjustment on the afternoon of July 2nd. E5 RON92 gasoline was cut by VND 1,055/liter (new ceiling: VND 19,730/liter), E10 RON95-III fell VND 788/liter (ceiling: VND 20,415/liter), diesel declined VND 690/liter (ceiling: VND 21,176/liter), and mazut (fuel oil) dropped VND 977/kg (ceiling: VND 14,053/kg). Notably, this is the second fuel price adjustment within a single week — the prior revision on the evening of July 1st had actually *raised* prices significantly (E5 RON92 up VND 1,426/liter). Authorities replenished the price stabilization fund (drawing on temporary budget advances) at VND 200/liter for gasoline and diesel and VND 400/kg for mazut, but opted not to draw from the fund to subsidize prices. **Relevance:** Fuel price volatility has a direct bearing on Vietnam's CPI trajectory. A net downward move in retail fuel prices, if sustained, could provide modest disinflationary relief — a mildly supportive signal for SBV to maintain or ease its policy stance, and marginally positive for bond duration. Traders should monitor the next adjustment cycle for confirmation of trend direction.
